evidence: Cic. Prov. Cons. 3: mīlitēs populī Rōmānī incūriā, fame, morbō … cōnsūmptī (Lewis & Short)
Hor. Ars 352: maculae quās aut incūria fūdit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “Through carelessness” is the plain ablative incūriā, as in Cicero, or per incūriam.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 27, checked against the searchable text of the book.
